newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Fahey says Telstra float on track.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Fahey says Telstra float on track.

text.p: Australian Finance Minister John Fahey said on Monday the government was still on track to float a third of its telecommunication carrier Telstra Corp by the end of calendar 1997.
He told reporters all the pre-float preparations were on schedule and the government would make a final decision later in the year about the definite float timing.
Fahey said the government would take into account market conditions at the time so as to maximise the government return.
"Whether we actually go to the market this year will depend on market conditions and what will optimise the return to the taxpayers of Australia," he said.

Last week Merill Lynch and County NatWest were named co-lead managers for the Australia tranche, Merrill Lynch and Salomon Brothers for the American tranche, Paribas and Cazenove for the U.K. and Europe, and HSBC James Capel for the rest of the world tranche.
Co-managers for the Australian tranche are BT Stockbroking, Prudential Bache and HSBC James Capel.
Co-managers for the American tranche are JP Morgan and Morgan Stanley.
